original.apparatus_description: A deterministic calculation interface for noisy qubit Pauli Z/X measurements on a fixed maximally entangled input, reporting the raw pre-clipping coherence-witness quantity.

common_fixed_conditions: The shared input is the maximally entangled qubit state (|00>+|11>)/sqrt(2), with theta=pi/4. Alice's two measurement settings are the Pauli Z and X eigenprojectors, with the submitted w used in each effect M^w=(1-w)Pi+w I/2.

The coherence reference basis is B_beta={|b_0>,|b_1>}, where |b_0>=cos(beta/2)|0>+sin(beta/2)|1> and |b_1>=-sin(beta/2)|0>+cos(beta/2)|1>. The angle beta is in [0,pi/4], is not a queryable control or a disclosed value, and stays fixed throughout an instance; different instances may have different beta.

For normalized conditional states rho_(a|x)=sigma_(a|x)/p(a|x), sigma_(a|x)=Tr_A[(M^w_(a|x) tensor I)|Phi+><Phi+|] and p(a|x)=Tr(sigma_(a|x)). Squared-l2 coherence is N(rho;B_beta)=sum_(i!=j)|<b_i|rho|b_j>|^2, and F_N is its concave roof over pure-state decompositions of rho.

The raw reported quantity is max_x sum_a p(a|x)N(rho_(a|x);B_beta) minus min_x sum_a p(a|x)F_N(rho_(a|x);B_beta), evaluated at the fixed input and reference basis. common_fixed_conditions: A low-viscosity liquid drop of radius R_d impacts a layer of the same liquid at speed V. The regime is the early two-jets splash, where the toroidal rim at the edge of the radially ejected liquid sheet produces spray.

The control is the dimensionless Weber number We = rho V^2 R_d / sigma. Here rho is liquid density, mu is dynamic viscosity, and sigma is surface tension. The fixed Ohnesorge number is Oh = mu / sqrt(rho R_d sigma) = 0.0105, and Re = sqrt(We) / Oh is large throughout the declared domain.
The layer depth is fixed at H/R_d = 1.8. The gas-to-liquid density ratio is 0.001 and the gas-to-liquid dynamic-viscosity ratio is 0.018. These conditions remain fixed as We varies.

The model describes incompressible early impact with an irrotational bulk outside thin viscous interfacial layers, while retaining viscous and capillary effects in the rim-ejection prediction. It is restricted to the stated spray regime and the declared query domain.

The readouts describe the toroidal rim at dimensionless time t_0 = 0.07, with time measured in units of R_d/V from nominal liquid contact in the absence of gas cushioning. By this time the rim has been ejected and its radial motion is ballistic; its diameter includes early rim thickening.
The reference response is a calibrated approximation for this regime. Both deterministic readouts refer to the toroidal rim; no additional conversion to secondary-droplet dimensions is included.

source_reference_settings: REFERENCE MODEL ONLY (defines the source-supported relation; an authored instance is not asserted to obey this Hamiltonian or energy constraint at the commanded fields): The apparatus is a deterministic theoretical calculation for the thermodynamic mean-field description of a uniform all-to-all three-spin model. The microscopic system has N spin-1/2 sites, with Pauli operators sigma_x and sigma_z whose eigenvalues are +1 and -1. Define X=sum_i sigma_x_i and Z=sum_i sigma_z_i. A fixed positive three-spin interaction coefficient J3 sets the energy unit. The Hamiltonian is H/J3=Z^3/N^2+hz*Z+hx*X, with no two-spin interaction term. The listed hx and hz are the known transverse and longitudinal field coefficients divided by J3, so both input numbers are dimensionless.

REFERENCE MODEL ONLY (defines the source-supported relation; an authored instance is not asserted to obey this Hamiltonian or energy constraint at the commanded fields): Use the uniform product-density-matrix mean-field model in the thermodynamic limit: rho=the tensor product over all sites of rho_i, where rho_i=[I+m*cos(alpha)*sigma_z+m*sin(alpha)*sigma_x]/2, 0<=m<=1 and 0<=alpha<2*pi. Equivalently, the single-spin Bloch components are z=m*cos(alpha), x=m*sin(alpha), with x^2+z^2=m^2<=1 and zero y component. These are Pauli-magnetization components per spin, not angular-momentum components with eigenvalues +/-1/2. No particular orientation alpha is fixed in advance.

REFERENCE MODEL ONLY (defines the source-supported relation; an authored instance is not asserted to obey this Hamiltonian or energy constraint at the commanded fields): In this model the energy density in the fixed natural unit is epsilon=E/(N*J3)=z^3+hz*z+hx*x. The entropy per spin, divided by the Boltzmann constant, is s(m)=ln(2)-[(1-m)*ln(1-m)+(1+m)*ln(1+m)]/2, with the continuous convention 0*ln(0)=0 at the boundary. These full expressions specify the thermodynamic model. No term is omitted from the energy, and all logarithms in this entropy definition are natural.

REFERENCE MODEL ONLY (defines the source-supported relation; an authored instance is not asserted to obey this Hamiltonian or energy constraint at the commanded fields): For any trial energy epsilon, the microcanonical state is found by maximizing this entropy over the entire allowed single-spin density-matrix set under that exact energy constraint. Because the entropy decreases with m, this also minimizes m at fixed energy. Compare global maxima; an arbitrary stationary point or local maximum is insufficient. This is the microcanonical energy-constrained problem, not a canonical free-energy minimization at a supplied temperature.
